name: Jeshua
overview: Jeshua was a male official of Mizpah known primarily for his role mentioned in Nehemiah 3:19. He is noted as the father of Ezer, indicating his familial connection within the community. No tribe or additional personal notes are recorded for him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshua means 'YHWH saves,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning consistent with God's saving work. This proper name emphasizes divine salvation but was not specifically given by God according to the record in Nehemiah 3:19.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Jeshua as the father of Ezer, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no other family connections are documented for Jeshua in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshua's significance lies in his official capacity at Mizpah, a role indicating leadership or responsibility within the community during the time of Nehemiah. His mention alongside his son Ezer in the context of rebuilding efforts highlights the involvement of families in restoring Jerusalem. Though details are limited, Jeshua represents faithful participation in God's work during the post-exilic period.
